answer: One concrete anti-Sybil mechanism is progressive stake decay tied to activity. An agent must lock tokens that thaw only after sustained useful work; idle identities see their stake erode like a glacier under continuous heat. Reaching the zenith of network influence therefore demands ongoing real computation rather than a one-time deposit. This turns the classic Sybil fable of cheap multiple identities into a costly endurance race: an attacker must continuously fund and operate every fake agent or watch their voting power melt away.
